subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis's 2010 Heroic Age Avengers with John Romita Jr., running to Avengers vs. X-Men.

subject: series
synopsis: Collected volumes of the Hell on Earth mega-arc, BPRD's apocalyptic final chapter spanning dozens of issues.
author: Mike Mignola

subject: series
synopsis: Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata's insider look at the manga industry, following two high school boys working toward serialization in Shonen Jump. A love story and career odyssey that demystifies the creative process while celebrating dedication and craft.
author: Tsugumi Ohba

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Snyder and Greg Capullo's New 52 Batman story in which Bruce Wayne discovers the Court of Owls, a secret society that has ruled Gotham for centuries.

subject: series
synopsis: A Black Label limited series written and drawn by Rafael Grampa presenting a psychologically intense Batman story with a striking art style exploring obsession, violence, and identity.
author: Rafael Grampa

subject: series
synopsis: Kentaro Yabuki's action manga following Train Heartnet, a former elite assassin called Black Cat who renounces killing to become a lighthearted bounty hunter. Known for its kinetic action sequences, charming cast, and Yabuki's expressive character designs; a staple of the mid-2000s Weekly Shonen Jump lineup.
author: Kentaro Yabuki

subject: series
synopsis: The sequel to Naruto follows Boruto Uzumaki, son of the Seventh Hokage, and his generation of young ninja navigating a world transformed by technology and his father's legacy. More divisive than its predecessor but escalates considerably in its Kara arc.
author: Masashi Kishimoto, Ukyô Kodachi

subject: series
synopsis: Roy Thomas and Scott Shaw's DC series stars Captain Carrot and his Amazing Zoo Crew, a team of funny-animal superheroes on the cartoon world of Earth-C. A lighthearted, pun-filled all-ages superhero parody.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Joyner's 1994 Damage: Grant Emerson, a teen with explosive powers, searches for his origins, later revealed as the Golden Age Atom's son.
author: Tom Joyner

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Cornell's New 52 medieval fantasy team book set in the Dark Ages with Etrigan the Demon, Madame Xanadu, Vandal Savage and other immortal characters.
author: Paul Cornell

subject: series
synopsis: Collection of Disney comic stories featuring Mickey, Donald, and other classic characters.

subject: series
synopsis: Drawn & Quarterly's foundational literary comics anthology, publishing early work by Seth, Joe Matt, Julie Doucet, and Chester Brown. The anthology that launched one of comics' most important independent publishers and defined the Canadian alt-comics movement.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: George Gately's long-running newspaper strip featuring Heathcliff, a wisecracking orange cat who outsmarted dogs and dominated his neighborhood. The strip ran from 1973 and was continued by Gately's nephew Peter Gallagher after George's death in 2001.
author: George Gately

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Mignola's genre-defining series following the demon son of a witch and a fallen angel, raised by American paranormal researchers and now humanity's best defense against occult threats — drawing on world mythology, folklore, and Lovecraftian horror with extraordinary atmosphere.
author: Mike Mignola

subject: series
synopsis: John Byrne's 1997 continuation of Kirby's Fourth World: Orion, Highfather, Darkseid and the New Gods in a 20-issue series.

subject: series
synopsis: Jean Van Hamme and Philippe Francq's Belgian thriller follows Largo Winch, the secret heir to a vast financial empire, navigating corporate espionage and international intrigue. A tightly plotted thriller series with great visual storytelling.
author: Jean Van Hamme

subject: series
synopsis: Fabien Vehlmann and Gwen de Bonneval's French sci-fi series drawn by Hervé Tanquerelle: a crook revives the last giant Atlas robot as an alien threat looms over Earth.

subject: series
synopsis: All-ages digest reimagining of Stan Lee and Steve Ditko's earliest Amazing Spider-Man stories, updated with contemporary dialogue while preserving the original plots. A lighthearted entry point for younger readers into Spider-Man's classic adventures.
author: Paul Tobin

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Gillis's continuation of the popular Micronauts licensed comics series, following the team through new cosmic adventures after the original series concluded. The data identifier suffix marks a specific scan of this issue set.
author: Peter Gillis

subject: series
synopsis: Yoshimurakana's violent crime manga follows Kuroko Koumori, a female serial killer who was given a deal to serve as an assassin for the police rather than face execution. Extremely violent, sexually explicit, and unapologetically trashy in an intentional way.
author: Yoshimurakana

subject: series
synopsis: Christophe Bec and Stefano Raffaele's French sci-fi graphic novel series exploring alien contact and its catastrophic consequences for human civilization. Thirteen volumes of escalating cosmic horror, with Raffaele's detailed, cinematic panels anchoring the speculative premise.
author: Christophe Bec

subject: series
synopsis: Infinity Comics vertical-scroll adaptation of Skottie Young's 2016 Rocket Raccoon & Groot.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Ed Brubaker's covert Avengers squad is sleek spy-thriller material. Warren Ellis's twelve-issue run that followed is even better — cinematic, efficient, and brutally clever.
author: Ed Brubaker

subject: series
synopsis: EC Comics' crime and social commentary anthology combining twist-ending suspense with pointed critiques of racism, antisemitism, and mob violence — unusually morally engaged for its era.
author: Al Feldstein

subject: series
synopsis: An anthology-format series featuring Hawkeye-led stories alongside rotating solo backups spotlighting supporting Avengers members, later renamed Avengers Spotlight. A useful vehicle for lesser-seen characters of the late 1980s.
author: Tom DeFalco

subject: series
synopsis: The complete collection of Dan Slott's Superior Spider-Man, in which Doctor Octopus takes over Peter Parker's body and attempts to be a better Spider-Man, creating one of the most controversial and compelling Spider-Man stories in decades.
author: Dan Slott

subject: series
synopsis: Digital-first DC comics featuring the older Superman of the Batman Beyond future, part of the Batman Beyond Unlimited initiative. Expands the animated universe's future DC with this era's version of the Man of Steel alongside the next generation of heroes.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2020 digital-first anthology series featuring standalone Superman stories by rotating creative teams, providing accessible entry points to the character.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Kirkman's story of a wealthy businessman turned werewolf who decides to use his affliction for good, only to find himself framed for murder and hunted by both heroes and villains. Connected to the Invincible universe.
author: Robert Kirkman

subject: series
synopsis: Steven T. Seagle and Kelley Jones' Vertigo series set in a world where a medieval Order of Crusaders secretly operates into the modern era, maintaining ancient secrets. Seagle's interest in institutional religion and Jones' atmospheric horror art combine effectively.
author: Steven T. Seagle

subject: series
synopsis: Immortal Hulk collection continuing the horror saga.
author: Al Ewing

subject: series
synopsis: Children at an idyllic orphanage discover a horrifying truth about their existence and plan an escape. Shirai and Demizu's manga delivers one of the most gripping first arcs in recent shonen history, though its later volumes are uneven.
author: Kaiu Shibuya

subject: series
synopsis: Ryan North and Erica Henderson's beloved Unbeatable Squirrel Girl omnibus or collected edition, gathering the delightfully comedic adventures of Doreen Green, a computer science student who defeats any villain with the power of squirrels and kindness.
author: Ryan North

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Taylor's 2023-2024 DC crossover event follows the Titans as a threat unleashed from Beast Boy threatens to transform the world's population. Taylor's sharp character work and escalating stakes make this a stronger-than-average DC event series.
author: Tom Taylor

subject: series
synopsis: Asao Takamori and Tetsuya Chiba's seminal manga about a troubled delinquent who becomes a passionate boxer. A raw, emotionally devastating classic that defined the boxing sports manga genre and left an indelible mark on Japanese popular culture.
author: Asao Takamori

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's revival of the classic Warren Publishing horror icon features the vampiric alien heroine in modern horror adventures. Multiple creative teams over the years produced uneven results, with standout runs from writers like Priest offering genuinely fresh takes on the character, though the title often prioritised pin-up aesthetics over storytelling.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Gregg Hurwitz's post-Dark Reign Moon Knight revamp. Marc Spector trying to be a 'good' hero while his Khonshu connection strains against that — effective psychological superhero material.
author: Gregg Hurwitz

subject: series
synopsis: Fawcett's 1940 anthology that introduced Captain Marvel (Billy Batson), one of the most important Golden Age comics titles, and source of characters later absorbed into DC.
author: Bill Parker

subject: series
synopsis: Derib and Job's Franco-Belgian children's comic series about a young Sioux boy with the ability to talk to animals; gentle, charming, and educational, widely popular in Europe as a children's classic.
author: Derib, Job

subject: series
synopsis: Naoki Urasawa's sprawling mystery manga spanning decades of plot threads, blending historical mystery with supernatural elements as conspiracies unfold across time.
author: Naoki Urasawa

subject: series
synopsis: Kazuo Koike and Goseki Kojima's companion series to Lone Wolf and Cub, following Yamada Asaemon, the official executioner to the Tokugawa shogunate, as he tests condemned men's blades and grapples with questions of death, justice, and humanity. Dark, philosophically rich gekiga at the height of the form.
author: Kazuo Koike

subject: series
synopsis: J.M. DeMatteis returns to his classic Spider-Man territory in this limited series exploring the Green Goblin's psychological shadow over Peter Parker's life. DeMatteis brings the same character insight that defined his legendary 1980s run.
author: J.M. DeMatteis

subject: series
synopsis: The Hernandez brothers' second Love and Rockets series (2001-2007): Jaime's Maggie and Hopey stories and Gilbert's Palomar-spun tales in standard comic format.

subject: series
synopsis: Jack Cole's Plastic Man in his own Quality title (1943-1956): elastic slapstick crimebusting with Woozy Winks; CV links the 1966 DC revival.

subject: series
synopsis: Duane Swierczynski's New 52 Birds of Prey: Black Canary leads Starling, Katana, Poison Ivy and later Batgirl as a fugitive covert team.

subject: series
synopsis: Jeph Loeb and Ed McGuinness's 2013 Nova: teenage Sam Alexander inherits his father's Nova helmet, continued by Zeb Wells and Gerry Duggan.
author: Zeb Wells

subject: series
synopsis: James Robinson and Leonard Kirk's 2015 Squadron Supreme: survivors of destroyed worlds form a ruthless team in the main Marvel Universe.

subject: series
synopsis: Kara Zor-L's various solo series. The Jimmy Palmiotti/Amanda Conner run is a delight — funny, confident, and a celebration of the character. Later runs are more variable.
author: Jimmy Palmiotti, Amanda Conner

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024 Marvel series featuring a new host for the Venom symbiote following the events that concluded Eddie Brock's long run as Venom. The new direction explores the symbiote's continuing evolution beyond its most famous human partner.

subject: series
synopsis: Muneyuki Kaneshiro and Akeji Fujimura's horror-survival manga following a new group of students forced to play deadly games controlled by gods and mythological beings — a direct sequel to their original series. Escalates the grotesque creativity of the first series with even more elaborate life-or-death game scenarios.
author: Muneyuki Kaneshiro

subject: series
synopsis: Allan Heinberg and Jim Cheung's long-delayed but beautifully drawn series following the Young Avengers seeking the Scarlet Witch to restore mutantkind, culminating in the death of the Vision's human persona and Scott Lang's return. A definitive Young Avengers story.
author: Allan Heinberg

subject: series
synopsis: Trade collections of Jason Aaron's ambitious and sprawling Avengers run, which expanded the team's scope to prehistoric times and cosmic scales, introducing the Avengers of 1,000,000 BC and pitting Earth's Mightiest Heroes against existential threats.
author: Jason Aaron

subject: series
synopsis: Yoshida Akimi's 1985 crime epic follows Ash Lynx, a teenage gang leader in New York, as he unravels the secret of a mysterious substance called Banana Fish. A rare shojo manga with the grit of crime noir and a deeply moving central relationship.
author: Akimi Yoshida

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Aaron's 2023 limited series stranding Bruce Wayne in deep space without his tech, forcing him to survive with pure wit and will among alien civilizations. A classic 'Batman without his toys' premise executed on a cosmic scale, exploring what makes the Dark Knight formidable apart from his gadgets.
author: Jason Aaron

subject: series
synopsis: A high school delinquent discovers oil painting and becomes obsessed with the Tokyo University of the Arts, one of Japan's most competitive art schools. A meticulous, emotionally honest manga about creative ambition and the labor behind artistic skill.
author: Tsubasa Yamaguchi

subject: series
synopsis: DC's biweekly series following twelve heroes and villains resurrected by the White Lantern entity, each bound to a mission tied to the return of a greater threat to Earth. A sprawling ensemble story that rewards patience with strong character moments.
author: Geoff Johns, Peter Tomasi

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Epic Collection paperbacks reprinting classic Captain America material in large affordable volumes, spanning the full history from golden-age through modern-era stories. An excellent way to read landmark Cap stories in comprehensive chronological format.
author: Various (Stan Lee, Jack Kirby, Roger Stern)

subject: series
synopsis: Al Ewing's politically sharp series follows Sam Wilson's Captain America leading a diverse Avengers squad, weaving social commentary about race, corporate power, and heroic responsibility into superhero action.
author: Al Ewing

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Carey's supernatural thriller about twins born at midnight in Nagasaki—one unable to be harmed by blades, one vulnerable to them—drawn into the world of Japanese spirits. Atmospheric and underrated.
author: Mike Carey

subject: series
synopsis: A continuation of Tom Taylor's Dark Knights of Steel — the DC Elseworlds setting that transplants DC heroes into a medieval fantasy world — with a winter war expansion that deepens the world-building and introduces new threats to the kingdom of the Els.
author: Tom Taylor

subject: series
synopsis: An indie comic series exploring themes of representation and governance through a speculative fiction lens.

subject: series
synopsis: Karl Bollers' limited series traces Emma Frost's backstory from troubled socialite to the White Queen, exploring her telepathic awakening and early criminal career before she became a full X-Men villain. A sympathetic origin for one of Marvel's most complex characters.
author: Karl Bollers

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Epic Collection paperbacks reprinting classic Fantastic Four stories chronologically, including the crucial Lee-Kirby period and key later runs by Byrne and Waid that defined the team across different eras.
author: Various (Stan Lee, John Byrne, Mark Waid)

subject: series
synopsis: AC Comics' anthology celebrating the 'good girl' art tradition of classic comics, featuring pin-up style artwork of heroic women in the tradition of Golden Age illustrators like Matt Baker and Bill Ward.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Bagge's 1990 Hate: slacker Buddy Bradley's misadventures in grunge-era Seattle and back home in New Jersey, a defining alternative humor comic.

subject: series
synopsis: Zeb Wells' sharp-tongued X-Men series places Mister Sinister in charge of Krakoa's most troublesome mutants — Psylocke, Wild Child, Greycrow, Nanny, Orphan-Maker, and others — on a team explicitly designed to do the morally questionable work the X-Men won't. Darkly funny and surprisingly character-rich.
author: Zeb Wells

subject: series
synopsis: Fujino Omori's manga spin-off from the main DanMachi series focusing on Aiz Wallenstein and the Loki Familia's perspective, revealing layers of the same events unseen in the primary narrative. Offers a worthwhile alternative viewpoint for fans of the main series.
author: Fujino Omori

subject: series
synopsis: Roy Thomas and John Buscema's 1980 King Conan: the aging Cimmerian rules Aquilonia, battling sorcery and usurpers alongside his son Conn.
author: Roy Thomas, Doug Moench

subject: series
synopsis: Kenzer & Company's collected editions of the long-running Knights of the Dinner Table comic strip by Jolly Blackburn, following a group of tabletop RPG players whose gaming sessions descend into rule-lawyering chaos, petty arguments, and genuine friendship. A cult classic beloved by tabletop gaming communities for its pitch-perfect insider humor.
author: Jolly Blackburn

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's continuation of its Robert E. Howard adaptation series, following Kull the Conqueror as he consolidates power over Valusia and faces supernatural threats. Part of Marvel's Bronze Age sword-and-sorcery line alongside Conan.
author: Don Glut

subject: series
synopsis: Shinobu Ohtaka's adventure manga set in a fantasy world inspired by One Thousand and One Nights, following Alibaba and the powerful Magi Aladdin as they explore mysterious dungeons and navigate political conflicts between nations. Ambitious worldbuilding with strong character work.
author: Shinobu Ohtaka

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Moore's revolutionary reimagining of Marvelman/Miracleman deconstructed the superhero genre with philosophical rigour and brutal consequences; Moore's run and Neil Gaiman's subsequent continuation are foundational texts of mature superhero comics.
author: Alan Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Ernie Bushmiller's classic newspaper strip featuring the gap-toothed, round-headed Nancy and her scruffy friend Sluggo in brilliantly minimalist daily gags. Celebrated by critics and comics theorists — most famously Scott McCloud — for Bushmiller's uncanny ability to convey maximum information and clarity in the fewest possible lines. A touchstone of the medium's formal possibilities.
author: Ernie Bushmiller

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2014 crossover event featuring the murder of Uatu the Watcher and the revelation of secrets across the Marvel universe. The main series effectively used its central mystery while spawning numerous tie-ins of varying quality.
author: Jason Aaron

subject: series
synopsis: Jamie Delano's supernatural crime thriller about a cursed American family — the Stories — bound together across generations by a legacy of violence and a living curse that shapes their destiny.
author: Jamie Delano

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's official Overwatch comics provide backstory and lore for characters from Blizzard's popular team-shooter game, covering events between the game's in-world history beats.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Peyer's 1994 R.E.B.E.L.S., continuing L.E.G.I.O.N.: Vril Dox's ousted team fights to retake the interstellar police force.
author: Tom Peyer

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Tomasi's 2024 DC series pairs Damian Wayne and Lor-Zod (son of General Zod) in an unlikely partnership, examining what it means to transcend your parents' legacies — villain and hero alike.
author: Peter Tomasi

subject: series
synopsis: Christopher Cantwell's 2023 IDW companion to Star Trek: Worf leads an outlaw crew including Spock and B'Elanna Torres aboard the Defiant.

subject: series
synopsis: Terry Moore's long-running series about the complex friendship, love, and lives of Francine and Katchoo — two women navigating relationships, careers, and a conspiracy from Katchoo's past — is one of the most beloved independent comics of its era.
author: Terry Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Kore Yamazaki's manga about a young woman sold at auction to a mysterious non-human sorcerer who intends to make her his bride and apprentice. A gorgeous, melancholy fairy tale steeped in British folklore and themes of belonging and identity.
author: Kore Yamazaki

subject: series
synopsis: Jun Mochizuki's steampunk fantasy manga set in a 19th-century Paris coexisting with vampires, following a vampire hunter partnered with the mysterious Vanitas who wields a legendary grimoire. Elegant art and intricate plotting in the Pandora Hearts tradition.
author: Jun Mochizuki

subject: series
synopsis: The flagship UK horror magazine (1976-1984) based on Hammer Films, featuring comic adaptations of Hammer movies alongside text features and interviews. Essential reading for fans of British horror cinema, with art that ranges from competent to genuinely atmospheric.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Neil Gaiman's foundational Vertigo series is one of the greatest comics works in the medium. Morpheus, Lord of Dreams, oversees a narrative that encompasses mythology, literature, history, and the nature of storytelling itself.
author: Neil Gaiman

subject: series
synopsis: An unusual DC series following a team of villains — Gorilla Grodd, Lex Luthor, and others — as protagonists. Ahead of its time in exploring moral ambiguity from the antagonist's perspective.

subject: series
synopsis: Reprint collections of Walt Simonson's seminal Thor run — widely considered the definitive Thor comics work — alongside Lee/Kirby foundational material, making essential mythological superhero storytelling accessible.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: A teen action-comedy series from Acclaim's revamp of the Valiant universe featuring a group of misfits with special abilities. Part of the late-1990s effort to reposition the Valiant properties toward a younger demographic.

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Abnett and Andy Lanning's cosmic Marvel event depicting war between the Shi'ar Empire and the Kree-Inhumans alliance. The peak of the Abnett/Lanning cosmic run — spectacular space opera with genuine emotional stakes.
author: Dan Abnett, Andy Lanning

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2024 What If anthology exploring alternate-universe scenarios featuring the Venom symbiote bonded with various unexpected Marvel characters — Wolverine, Thor, Punisher, and others — in standalone what-if stories. A fun format for symbiote fans.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Aaron's pre-Schism Wolverine series collecting the Weapon X, Insane in the Brain, and Tomorrow Dies Today arcs, establishing Aaron's confident voice for the character before his landmark Wolverine & X-Men run.
author: Rick Remender

subject: series
synopsis: The continuation of Chris Claremont's alternate-universe X-Men series, picking up in his imagined 1990s timeline where the X-Men never evolved past his original run. A nostalgic what-if that rewards longtime Claremont readers.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: Yoshihiro Togashi's manga about a delinquent teenager who becomes an underworld detective after dying and being resurrected. Begins as a ghost story but evolves into an inventive tournament fighting manga with genuine emotional complexity and Togashi's trademark imaginative power systems.
author: Yoshihiro Togashi

subject: series
synopsis: Chip Zdarsky and Marco Checchetto's 2022 Daredevil after Devil's Reign: Matt and Elektra lead the Fist against the Hand, closing Zdarsky's run.

subject: series
synopsis: John Byrne's 2004 Doom Patrol reboot, ignoring prior continuity: Robotman, Elasti-Girl and Negative Man with new members Nudge, Grunt and Vortex.

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Valentino's Image title about an HIV-positive anti-hero. Noble intentions hampered by the era's excess — the social messaging lands harder than the storytelling.
author: Jim Valentino

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1989 ongoing series for Helena Bertinelli, the new Huntress — a Mafia don's daughter who became a vigilante after witnessing her family's assassination — establishing her as distinct from the Earth-2 original. The series built her civilian identity and her difficult relationship with Gotham's established heroes, particularly Batman.
author: Joey Cavalieri

subject: series
synopsis: Ka-Zar's first series (1974-1977), after Astonishing Tales; our files include Mark Waid and Andy Kubert's 1997 relaunch.
author: Doug Moench

subject: series
synopsis: Stan Lee and John Buscema's 1968 Silver Surfer: the exiled herald's philosophical, melancholy battles with Mephisto and humanity over 18 issues.

subject: series
synopsis: Jed MacKay's 2024 Moon Knight: Fist of Khonshu, Marc Spector's return after Vengeance of the Moon Knight.

subject: series
synopsis: Spencer Ackerman and Julius Ohta's 2024 Iron Man relaunch.

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman and Dustin Weaver's 2010 S.H.I.E.L.D.: a secret history of the Marvel Universe in which Leonardo da Vinci, Newton and Galileo guard the Earth.

subject: series
synopsis: She-Hulk volume 2 (2005-2009): Dan Slott's legal-comedy run continued, then Peter David's darker bounty-hunter turn.
author: Peter David

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1987 revived Strange Tales, a flip book of Cloak and Dagger and Doctor Strange, 19 issues.
author: Bill Mantlo, Peter B. Gillis

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2004 bi-monthly X-Men Unlimited: two short stories per issue by rotating creators.
author: Ted Naifeh

subject: series
synopsis: Graphic novels adapting the Italian children's series: newspaper-editor mouse Geronimo Stilton travels through history to stop the Pirate Cats.

subject: series
synopsis: Ryoko Fukuyama's music romance manga following Nino, a girl with a powerful voice whose connections to two childhood loves are mediated through music, pain, and the competitive world of the indie rock scene. A melodramatic but emotionally committed romance that found a devoted shojo audience.
author: Ryoko Fukuyama

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Russell's 2024 DC limited series set across different decades of Batman's career using the backdrop of the Civil Rights Movement, Vietnam, and Cold War to examine Bruce Wayne's vigilantism through a historical and political lens. Russell's satirical edge sharpens the examination of what Batman represents in each era.
author: Mark Russell

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first DC anthology expanding the Batman Beyond animated universe with Batman Beyond, Superman Beyond, and Justice League Beyond stories in parallel. Strong continuity with the animated series' tone and characters.

subject: series
synopsis: Tatsuki Fujimoto's anarchic action manga about Denji, a destitute devil hunter who merges with his chainsaw devil to become a human-devil hybrid working for a clandestine government agency. Subverts shonen conventions with nihilistic energy and genuine emotional devastation.
author: Tatsuki Fujimoto

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Moore, Garth Ennis, Christos Gage, Max Brooks, and Kieron Gillen's horror anthology set in a decaying movie theater where the films come to terrible life — a love letter to pulp horror traditions.
author: Alan Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Moore's Crossed continuation set 100 years after the infection's outbreak, following a group of survivors in a world that has adapted to the Crossed threat — Moore examining hope and civilization's resilience in the ruins.
author: Alan Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Fantagraphics' 17-volume chronological collection of R. Crumb's work, from early sketchbooks through Zap, Fritz the Cat, Mr. Natural and Weirdo.

subject: series
synopsis: A DC Black Label horror event series in which a secret vampire conspiracy has begun replacing DC heroes, as the remaining human heroes must uncover and fight the spreading undead plague.

subject: series
synopsis: Akira Toriyama's comedy classic introduces Arale, a super-strong robot girl built by the bumbling inventor Senbei Norimaki, in the gag-filled Penguin Village. Toriyama's pre-Dragon Ball work demonstrating his gift for visual comedy and warm-hearted absurdism.
author: Akira Toriyama

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Loren Fleming's 1992 ongoing following the dark entity Eclipso possessing various characters in an isolated mountain community, a horror-superhero hybrid that was unusually dark for its era.
author: Robert Loren Fleming

subject: series
synopsis: Hiroki Endo's ambitious cyberpunk epic set in a near-future ravaged by a plague follows Elijah, son of a legendary guerrilla fighter, navigating corporate wars, drug cartels, and questions of human identity. One of the most underrated and thematically rich manga of its era.
author: Hiroki Endo

subject: series
synopsis: Adam Warren's deconstructive superhero comedy-drama — originally begun as a series of sketch commissions — following Emp, a superheroine whose suit tears easily, leaving her perpetually captured, but whose personal growth and determination eventually make her genuinely formidable.
author: Adam Warren

subject: series
synopsis: Matt Fraction and Mark Bagley's 2013 Fantastic Four: the family's year-long voyage through space and time, companion to FF.

subject: series
synopsis: Cullen Bunn and Tyler Crook's Dark Horse series follows Emmy, a girl in a rural county who discovers she is tied to a murdered witch and to the haunts that stir in the surrounding hills. A Southern-gothic horror about inheritance, community, and buried evil.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: Brandon Thomas and Juan Gedeon's science fiction series told from the alien perspective — an advance scout from a world Earth plans to colonize arrives first to prevent the invasion, flipping the expected alien-invasion narrative.
author: Brandon Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Pak and Fred Van Lente's witty, mythologically rich series that grew out of World War Hulk, following Hercules and young genius Amadeus Cho on globe-trotting adventures through Greek, Norse, and other pantheons. One of Marvel's most underrated runs.
author: Greg Pak, Fred Van Lente

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns's 2005 sequel to Crisis on Infinite Earths, pitting Superboy-Prime and Alexander Luthor against the DC Universe in a battle over the nature of heroism and reality.
author: Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: Rumiko Takahashi's feudal fantasy follows Kagome, a modern girl pulled into the past, and Inuyasha, a half-demon, as they gather the shards of the Shikon Jewel while battling the demon Naraku. A defining manga of its era, beloved for its romantic tension and sprawling mythology.
author: Rumiko Takahashi

subject: series
synopsis: Nick Spencer's 2011 Iron Man 2.0: James Rhodes upgrades from War Machine to an intelligence-driven armor and investigates the death of Palmer Addley.

subject: series
synopsis: Don McGregor and Billy Graham's groundbreaking Black Panther stories in Jungle Action #6-24, featuring 'Panther's Rage' — widely considered the first extended superhero graphic novel — and 'Panther vs. the Klan,' bold sociopolitical storytelling far ahead of its time.
author: Don McGregor

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024 Marvel series featuring a new young Venom-adjacent character, part of Marvel's expansion of the symbiote mythology beyond the classic Eddie Brock and Venom concepts.

subject: series
synopsis: Boom Studios' comics set in the Magic: The Gathering universe, exploring the planeswalker mythology and multiple planes of the game's rich fantasy world.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's premium hardcover reprints of the classic Stan Lee–Gene Colan Daredevil stories — the foundational run that transformed Matt Murdock from an inferior Spider-Man into a genuine noir hero with a romantic sensibility all his own. Essential silver-age Marvel reading.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's all-ages companion comics to the Avengers: Earth's Mightiest Heroes animated series, featuring the team in adventures that match the show's character dynamics and tone.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first Infinite Comic series based on the Avengers Assemble animated series, delivering all-ages adventures for younger readers in the style of the popular cartoon.

subject: series
synopsis: Yoshiyuki Nishi's supernatural action manga following two young investigators — the brilliantly harsh Muhyo and his earnest assistant Roji — as they apply magical law to send ghosts and demons to justice. A clever procedural approach to supernatural manga with well-designed monsters and satisfying ghost-story resolutions.
author: Yoshiyuki Nishi

subject: series
synopsis: Ernie Bushmiller's legendary minimalist gag strip about the spiky-haired Nancy and her pal Sluggo; revered by comics theorists for its perfectly efficient joke construction, and brilliantly reinvented by Olivia Jaimes in 2018.
author: Ernie Bushmiller

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel horror series teaming Blade, Frank Drake, and Hannibal King as a monster-hunting unit operating in the darker corners of the Marvel Universe. Part of the Midnight Sons initiative, blending superhero action with supernatural horror.

synopsis: A Fantagraphics reprint volume collecting E.C. Segar's classic Thimble Theatre newspaper strips featuring Popeye, Olive Oyl, and the mysterious Jeep creature.
author: E.C. Segar

author: Kieron Gillen

synopsis: All-ages Marvel series retelling the earliest X-Men adventures with updated art and dialogue, revisiting the Lee and Kirby originals for new readers. Nostalgic and accessible, though narratively straightforward.

synopsis: Oni Press's licensed comic adaptation of the Adult Swim series maintains the anarchic, pop-science-fiction humour of the show with original interdimensional adventures. Written by Zac Gorman and a rotating cast of contributors, it's a solid companion piece for fans, though it naturally lacks the animated medium's timing and voice performances.
author: Zac Gorman

author: Kelly Thompson

synopsis: Infinity Comics vertical-scroll edition of Brian Michael Bendis and Leinil Francis Yu's 2008 Secret Invasion: the Skrulls' hidden infiltration of Earth's heroes.

synopsis: Jim Zub's fantasy action-comedy: two nameless mercenaries, a hulking man and a dwarf, stumble through assassination plots, undead and pirates for pay.

author: Kouji Seo
